allOf.description: Fail-closed rule (plan §5.3): a protected intent change classified unknown, unsupported, or incomparable blocks ordinary promotion pending review — the policy decision must be block or review.

classifier.$comment: RFC 0031 F3, paid here. The artifact recorded neither the classifier version nor the normal-form version, though both are part of the classification's identity under RFC 0030's query key — so a diff could be silently reused across a change that could have re-classified it. Mirrors RFC 0028's F3 on the context-pack side.
classifier.description: Identity of the classifier that produced this artifact (RFC 0031, "Inputs, preconditions, and determinism"). A diff MUST NOT be reused across an advance of any recorded component; a relation recorded as `unknown` under one classifier version may be recomputed by a later one, but the later result is a new `diff_*`, never an edit of this artifact (INV-009).

classifier_version.description: Version of the semantic/intent-diff classifier. It advances whenever a classification could change for any input.

cpnf_version.description: Canonical property normal form the expression comparisons were computed under — `cpnf-1` for the form RFC 0037 fixes. A new normal form does not silently re-classify history.

intent_changes.description: One record per classified unit that is not `unchanged` (RFC 0031). Two units with different relations MUST NOT be collapsed into one record, which is what makes the per-unit locator below load-bearing rather than decorative.

allOf.$comment: RFC 0031 F1, paid here. The record shape could not say *which* claim was weakened, and the classifier carried the unit identity only in `policy.reasons` prose — a machine-consumable fact living in a prose field is the INV-003 failure. The eleven fields listed here are exactly those whose RFC 0031 unit-of-classification table declares a per-unit key; the four omitted fields (`bounds`, `trust_boundaries`, `completion_policy`, `assurance`) are classified as a whole and have no sub-unit to name.
allOf.description: A field classified per unit names the unit it classified.

fragment.description: Declared semantic fragment (ADR-0025) the change's relation was classified in; outside declared fragments the relation is unsupported (RFC 0031).

protected.$comment: Fail-closed (review 5, A1): protection derives from the field enum — every member of `field` is in the RFC 0037 protected set, so a listed intent change is always protected. The constant keeps the wire shape while making an unprotected classification unrepresentable.

unit.description: Per-unit locator: the key of the classified unit within the record's `field`, per RFC 0031's unit-of-classification table. Claims, assumptions, and observers are keyed by `id`; abstraction maps by `role`; nondeterminism entries by `site`; fairness constraints by the (`kind`, `action`) pair, rendered `kind:action`; `scope` by the sub-field (`components`, `fragments`, `abstraction_level`); `faults` by the member of `enabled` or `profiles`; `optimization` and `non_vacuity` by the constraint, objective, or behavior; `security_policy` by `data_classification`, the redaction class, or the capability requirement. The contract path the key resolves against is the one `x-policy-field-map` relates the diff field to (intent-contract.schema.json).

decision.$comment: No `unknown` decision (review 5, A1): an unknown classification cannot be expressed as a structurally blocking decision in this artifact, so it fails closed to block or review at classification time.

reasons.$comment: RFC 0031 F4 remains open and is deferred, not paid: typing these reasons requires a closed per-field reason vocabulary, and RFC 0031 mints none — inventing one here would make this schema the source of a vocabulary the RFC does not define, which is the inverse of INV-003. It is an RFC 0031 revision, not a schema sweep. The half of F4 that was schema-side is paid instead by `intent_changes[].unit`: the unit identity these strings used to carry as prose now has a typed home, so a reason string is no longer the only place a machine-consumable fact appears.
reasons.description: Human-readable justifications for the decision. Rendering only: every fact a consumer acts on MUST also appear in a typed field (INV-003).

requested_assurance.$comment: RFC 0031 F2, paid here. The field was an unconstrained string while RFC 0031 requires one of the five AssuranceLevel tokens. The enum is token-for-token the `assurance.minimum` enum of intent-contract.schema.json and `AssuranceLevel` in crates/continuum-value/src/assurance.rs; reordering or renaming a member is a coordinated breaking change across RFC 0031, RFC 0037, that schema, and that crate.
requested_assurance.description: Requested assurance for the classification itself — the RFC 0031 diff input. It bounds the evidence the classifier may rely on to claim a direction: `observed` and `sampled` admit none, so every expression-level direction classifies `unknown`; a direction the classifier can support only with weaker evidence than requested MUST be reported as `unknown`, never as the direction. Relations decidable by canonical encoding alone do not consume this budget.

schema_id.description: Artifact-class identity of the governing schema: its `$id` with the `v<schema_epoch>/` segment removed (schemas/README.md). Stable across schema epochs.

schema_epoch.description: Schema epoch this instance was written against (schemas/README.md). It advances only on a breaking change to this artifact class, is not one of the six independently versioned epochs (RFC 0026 `rule versioning.epoch_independence`), and pins no semantics.

fragment.description: Declared semantic fragment (ADR-0025) the change was classified in (RFC 0031).
